note: Famous trees Commons has a category for and we do not map. Found by scripts/famous_trees.py; each one already has photographs and usually coordinates, so the expensive half of a research pass is done. Not verified by us, not published.

leads.name: 1000-jährige Eiche Bad Blumau
leads.why: Well documented tree, locally nicknamed 'die dicke Oachn', standing in Bierbaum an der Safen at the end of the Eichenweg toward Loimeth (municipality of Bad Blumau, Steiermark), on a private plot ('auf einem privaten Grundstück, Ortsende von Bierbaum, nach der kleinen Kapelle' per meinbezirk.at) but treated as a public attraction with marked trails, information signage and guided tours (per meinbezirk.at's Hartberg-Fuerstenfeld article, 'thousands of annual visitors'). Species and measurements from baumkunde.de's tree register (dendrology enthusiast database, last visited/measured 09.08.2018): Stiel-Eiche/Pedunculate Oak (Quercus robur), girth 8.75m (875cm) at that visit, height 30m, coordinates N47 6.32538' E16 2.94798' (converted: 47.105423, 16.049133), status 'vital' and 'öffentlich zugänglich' (publicly accessible). AGE IS DISPUTED, both figures kept rather than one picked: baumkunde.de gives 500-600 years as its own measurement-based estimate and explicitly flags this as contradicting the popular name; meinbezirk.at's Hartberg-Fuerstenfeld piece instead states 'Experten bestaetigen: rund 1.000 Jahre alt' and repeats the legend that it was 'allegedly planted around the year 1020'. No source states which experts or method reached the 1000-year figure, so it reads as the same unverified local tradition rather than an independent dendrological measurement; baumkunde's girth-based figure is more likely the sounder one but I am not picking a winner. Alive: meinbezirk (graz community edition) reports a lightning strike in the 1970s that was clumsily filled with concrete, causing decay, and a restoration in 1989 by tree surgeon Manfred Saller funded by a donation from Heidi Horten, after which 'the oldest oak in Europe shines again in full vitality'; baumkunde's 2018 visit independently confirms 'vital' condition. Clears the bar: alive and vital as of the two most recent checks (1989 restoration outcome, 2018 measurement), two independent sources for species/age/location that actually disagree on age (flagged rather than resolved), one collectible point, publicly reachable despite private ownership of the plot. Sources: https://www.baumkunde.de/baumregister/1309-tausendjaehrige_eiche_in_bad_blumau/ ; https://www.meinbezirk.at/hartberg-fuerstenfeld/c-lokales/die-1000-jaehrige-eiche-von-bierbaum_a7441969 ; https://www.meinbezirk.at/graz/c-regionauten-community/die-1000-jaehrige-eiche-in-bierbaum-gemeinde-bad-blumau_a5050954

leads.name: Birnbaum auf dem Walserfeld
leads.blocked_reason: Same failure as the Kaiserbuche, and for the same structural reason: this is a symbolic site repeatedly replanted since at least 1564 (sagen.at; de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birnbaum_auf_dem_Walserfeld), not a single old tree. De.wikipedia's own infobox lists it as an 'ehemaliges Naturdenkmal' (FORMER natural monument): the tree that held that status was planted in 1887 and stood until 2014/2015, then came down and was replaced; a new pear was planted in 2015 with a ceremonial dedication in 2016. The living tree today is roughly 10-11 years old, ordinary in size, ineligible as 'genuinely old' or 'visually spectacular'. The memorial plaque and local legends (tied to the Battle of Walserfeld, 1800, among older sagas) are about the SITE and the recurring planting, not about any one living specimen -- fails the destination test, since what draws a visit is the marker and the story, not a decade-old sapling. Both Austrian candidates in this file share this pattern and neither ships as a tree entry.

leads.name: Friedenslärche
leads.why: SALZBURGWIKI's own dedicated article (as 'Tettenbacher Friedenslärche') and a meinbezirk.at Regionauten piece agree independently: a larch planted in 1918 by a local farmer ('vom Tettenbacher Bauer') out of gratitude for returning safely home from the First World War ('zum Dank fuer seine glueckliche Heimkehr aus dem Ersten Weltkrieg'). It stands on the pilgrimage path (Maria-Buehel-Strasse) that climbs from Oberndorf's Stille-Nacht-Platz up to the Wallfahrtskirche Maria Buehel, near the Wasserkapelle Maria Buehel which itself sits a few hundred metres below the church. Species is given only as 'Laerche' (larch) in both sources, not to exact species; European Larch (Larix decidua) is the overwhelmingly likely native larch in this region and is used here as a reasonable default, not a confirmed identification, worth a reader question on the page. SALZBURGWIKI's broader 'Kleindenkmaeler und Kunstwerke in Oberndorf' page lists it among small monuments (Kleindenkmal), not among the separate Naturdenkmal category; a WebSearch AI summary claimed Naturdenkmal status but that word does not appear on either page actually fetched, so it is dropped per the search-summary-is-a-lead-never-a-source rule. No girth or height figure exists in any source found; age is well documented instead (planted 1918, so roughly 108 years old as of 2026), so age_estimate is set from the planting date rather than derived from girth. Alive: a Commons photograph dated 2022-04-21 (Rufus46, CC BY-SA 4.0) shows it standing and captioned as the 1918-planted peace larch; no coordinates embedded in the file. Location is APPROXIMATE: no source gives tree-level coordinates, only the stretch of Maria-Buehel-Strasse where the Wasserkapelle and tree stand, between the town centre and the church. Access: free, beside the public pilgrimage path/street, no permission or ticket needed. TRANSPORT NOTE for whoever decides its container later: straight-line distance from Oberndorf Bahnhof (47.9417, 12.9441) to the Wallfahrtskirche Maria Buehel (47.9500, 12.9262) is about 1.6km uphill via the Kalvarienbergstiege stairs; combined with the roughly 25-minute S-Bahn/regional train from Salzburg Hauptbahnhof, the one-way journey from central Salzburg runs to roughly 50-55 minutes door to tree, meaningfully past the project's ~30-minute day-trip boundary, so this reads as historically significant (a private WWI homecoming memorial) rather than a Salzburg-city entry; not my call to resolve, just recording it honestly. Clears the bar: alive, documented planting date giving a real age, two independent sources for existence/history, one collectible point, publicly reachable; the only soft points are the approximate pin and the unconfirmed exact species. Sources: https://wiki.sn.at/wiki/Tettenbacher_Friedensl%C3%A4rche ; https://www.meinbezirk.at/flachgau/c-regionauten-community/wallfahrtskirche-maria-buehel-oberndorf_a7215209 ; https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Friedenslaerche_Maria_Buehel_Oberndorf_bei_Salzburg-1.jpg
leads.container_decision: Decided 2026-09-18: NOT added to Salzburg. famous_map.py places it 18.6km straight-line from the city, but the verify pass measured the real one-way transit as roughly 50-55 minutes door to tree, well past the roughly-30-minute day-trip norm CLAUDE.md uses elsewhere (Blarney/Fota for Cork are 15-20 min). Kept as a fully-verified lead for a future Oberndorf bei Salzburg page (the Silent Night town) once more trees are found nearby it; do not re-add to Salzburg without new transit evidence.

leads.name: Kaiserbuche, Haunsberg
leads.blocked_reason: Not a collectible tree: the historic beech planted in 1779/1791 to mark Emperor Joseph II's 1779 visit to the Haunsberg fell in a storm in 2004 after 225 years as one of Salzburg's oldest natural monuments (de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaiserbuche_(Haunsberg); meinbezirk.at). Its replacement was destroyed by an act of vandalism in February 2008. A further replacement was planted in summer 2009 and stands today behind a 2-metre fence -- so the current living 'Kaiserbuche' is roughly 17 years old, unremarkable in size, and fenced off from close approach. The site (viewpoint, 1898 memorial chapel, 1779/1957 pyramid) is genuinely a hiking destination, but the LIVING TREE fails the destination test on its own merits: nobody travels for a 17-year-old sapling behind a fence. CAUTION for any future photo pass: the Commons photo 'Alte_Kaiserbuche_1/2.jpg' (Alte = old) almost certainly depicts the pre-2004 original tree that no longer exists, not the current living planting -- do not use it as a photo of an extant tree.

leads.name: Nonnenbuche, Gutenstein
leads.species_basis: confirmed by both Commons photo descriptions ('Rotbuche')
leads.why: Not enough to verify: only ONE real source exists so far, restated across three photo description pages rather than independent. All three Commons file pages (01, 02, checked directly) agree on the same single fact: an ordinary European beech carries a memorial plaque reading 'Hier sind 4 brave Nonnen mit Gottes Hilf dem Tod entronnen. 1966' (here 4 good nuns escaped death with God's help, 1966), photographed 2016-07-23 for WikiDaheim 2017, at approx 47.8763/15.8940 (the two photo pages give slightly different coordinates 30m apart, both near the lead's point). No age, girth, height, Naturdenkmal ID, or any account of WHAT actually happened in 1966 (what the nuns escaped, why this specific tree) was found anywhere: two WebSearches (general history, hiking-trail context) turned up nothing beyond the plaque text itself. Without a second, independent account of the 1966 event or any register/measurement data, this cannot clear the two-independent-sources bar for existence+history, and it is also unclear the tree itself (rather than the plaque) is the destination, since nothing suggests unusual age or size. Leaving as a lead rather than blocking outright: the plaque and photos are real, it just needs a local history source (Gutenstein municipality, a Wieneralpen/Bucklige Welt hiking guide, or a Niederoesterreich Naturdenkmal list) that a future pass has not yet found.

leads.name: Rehberger Kreuz, Hofamt Priel
leads.blocked_reason: Not a tree. Checked two of the three Commons file pages (01 and 03) directly: 'Das Rehberger Kreuz' is a wayside CROSS/shrine standing on the Wachaustrasse B3 at the Hofamt Priel/Persenbeug-Gottsdorf municipal boundary (coordinates 48d11'25.81"N 15d5'54.48"E, matching the lead's point), a former execution site of the regional court per one search snippet. Neither photo description, category list, nor structured data mentions any tree at all, species, age or size. This is a famous_trees.py false positive, almost certainly matched on the word 'Kreuz' or the surrounding Commons category rather than any tree content. Blocked as not a collectible tree entry; a future pass should not re-check this same candidate without new evidence a tree is actually involved.

leads.name: Bühler-Linde (Grünburg)
leads.species_basis: confirmed exact species by the Commons file's own categories ('Tilia platyphyllos in Austria')
leads.why: Checked the lead photo's Commons page directly: it names the tree's address as Heindlmuehlstrasse 1, Leonstein (Gemeinde Gruenburg), standing at the 'Bauernhof Hasenguetl (auch Buehler, Hoechtl)', a working FARM, which raises hard-rule-10 access questions the way the Rehberger/Kaiserbuche cases already show up in this file: no source found says whether the tree stands on the public road frontage or inside the farmyard proper. No age, girth or height figure exists on the Commons page and two WebSearches (a direct German search and a baumkunde.de-targeted search) found no baumkunde entry, register listing or news piece giving a second independent source for age/history at all -- only the one Commons description, restated across three photo filenames. Recorded as a lead needing both a second source and an access answer before it can verify; a future pass could try the OO Naturdenkmal list for Kirchdorf district or an OSM check on Heindlmuehlstrasse's road/farmyard boundary.

leads.name: Japanischer Schnurbaum, Bregenz
leads.species_basis: confirmed exact species by VOL.AT news article, which gives the latin synonym 'Styphnolobium japonicum' directly
leads.why: Two independent sources agree on the facts but NOT verified because ACCESS is unresolved, which is the one thing that stops this shipping. Vorarlberg's own 'Liste der Naturdenkmaeler im Bezirk Bregenz' (de.wikipedia, fetched as wikitext) lists it as ND-213, Gemeinde Bregenz, coordinates 47.4922093135/9.7241185644 (recorded above). VOL.AT (vol.at/japanischer-schnurbaum-jetzt-naturdenkmal/1730404, published 2010-07-02) independently confirms: declared a local Naturdenkmal by Bregenz's Stadtvertretung on 1 July 2010; planted 'vor 60 Jahren' (about 60 years before 2010, so roughly planted 1950, ~76 years old as of 2026); trunk 86cm thick (diameter, not girth: circumference is roughly pi*86 = 270cm), height 12.5m, crown diameter 26m; condition in 2010 was 'schwach geschaedigt, aber vital' (11-25% leaf loss, weakly damaged but vital) with traffic safety confirmed. A 2016 Wiki Loves Earth photograph (commons, CC BY-SA 4.0, dated 2016-05-30) is a second, more recent alive-confirmation. THE BLOCKER: both sources place it 'am Johann-Joerg-Weg beim Pausenhof der HS Rieden-Vorkloster', i.e. on/by the schoolyard of a Hauptschule (Rieden-Vorkloster). Hard rule 10's school exception requires real evidence the grounds are genuinely open (a public path crossing them, or the site bordering rather than being inside school grounds); the phrasing 'am Johann-Joerg-Weg' (ON the Weg/path) suggests the tree may stand on the path bordering the yard rather than inside a fenced enclosure, but no source states this plainly and two attempts to check via OpenStreetMap Overpass (overpass-api.de returned HTTP 406 twice, a kumi.systems mirror returned nothing within the timeout) did not settle it. A WebSearch on public accessibility returned no decisive answer either. Recorded here as an open access question rather than blocked outright, since inconvenience/uncertainty is not the same as confirmed harm: a future pass should check a street-level map or aerial image to see whether Johann-Joerg-Weg runs along the school's public side or through its fenced yard before deciding ship or block.
